title: AOO-ANFIS: A Novel Bio-Inspired Neuro-Fuzzy Controller for Hydrostatic Transmission Stroke Control
abstract: Hydrostatic transmissions (HSTs) rely on coordinated pump and motor displacement control to achieve smooth stroke regulation. This study proposes AOO-ANFIS, a bio-inspired neuro-fuzzy controller in which the 66 premise and consequent parameters of a two-input, two-output first-order Takagi–Sugeno adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) are tuned by the animated oat optimization (AOO) algorithm rather than by ANFIS’s conventional gradient-based hybrid learning rule. The controller is trained as a data-driven surrogate for a previously validated multiple model predictive controller (MMPC): closed-loop input–output samples generated by the MMPC are used as supervised targets, enabling the resulting fuzzy controller to reproduce the MMPC control policy without solving an online optimization problem. On this identical tuning task, AOO was benchmarked against Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO), particle swarm optimization (PSO), a real-coded genetic algorithm (GA) and the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES). It reached the lowest mean validation error, significantly lower than HHO, GA and CMA-ES and statistically indistinguishable from PSO. The AOO-ANFIS controller was subsequently deployed in a processor-in-the-loop simulation on a BeagleBone Black target, replacing the previously reported MMPC under identical deterministic and stochastic torque disturbance profiles. Relative to the MMPC, the AOO-ANFIS controller reduced the maximum overshoot from 25% to 14% under deterministic disturbances and from 24% to 14% under stochastic disturbances, reduced the closed-loop tracking RMSE by 7.8% and 30.1%, respectively, and reduced the integral squared-error indices ISE and ITSE by 15% and 21% under deterministic and by 51% and 41% under stochastic disturbances. It did so with an average control effort about 10 percentage lower and an average computational load 76–84% lower, at the cost of a longer peak time under stochastic disturbances: 1.8 s instead of 1 s. In an extended 300 s scenario containing reference levels, ramp rates, a sinusoidal segment and trapezoidal disturbances absent from the training data, the AOO-ANFIS maintained bounded tracking with an RMSE of 0.035 over the unseen segment, lower than that of a previously published ANN surrogate trained on the same data, 0.056. Both surrogates remained stable when the plant’s volumetric-efficiency maps were degraded by about 15%, with the AOO-ANFIS showing lower error. Moreover, this is the first application of the AOO algorithm to ANFIS tuning and the first bio-inspired-optimization-tuned ANFIS controller for HST stroke control.

title: Nova: A Real-Time AI Sales Call Assistant with Live Speech Transcription, Knowledge-Grounded Coaching and Simulated Sales Training
abstract: Sales representatives must respond to customers in real time while recalling product details, recognizing customer needs and buying signals, and deciding on suitable follow-up actions. This paper presents Nova, a full-stack Real-Time AI Sales Call Assistant that supports representatives during customer conversations. The browser captures live speech through the Web Speech API and converts it into a running transcript, and the React frontend sends the relevant conversation data to a Flask backend through REST APIs. An AI coaching service analyzes the conversation context and returns live suggestions, namely a recommended response, a follow-up question, objection-handling guidance, detected buying signals and a next action. Lead management, call history, call notes, follow-ups, a dashboard and follow-up email workflows are supported using SQLite and SQLAlchemy with JWT-based authentication. A training module simulates customer scenarios and scores the practice session. Completed calls store the transcript, call duration, speaker information, sentiment, summary and follow-up recommendations. The implemented system supports live microphone capture, speech transcription, real-time coaching suggestions, lead management and call-history storage. The current coaching logic is built around rules, knowledge and application logic, and no formal predictive-model accuracy is reported. The system integrates live transcription, coaching, record keeping and training within a single web application.

title: Multi-Objective Dhole Optimization for Saturation-Aware Autonomous Underwater Forensic Search and Evidence Recovery Missions
abstract: Background: Underwater forensic investigations frequently involve searching, locating, and recovering submerged human remains and associated forensic evidence under challenging environmental conditions. Efficient coordination of multiple unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs) can support forensic investigators by reducing search time, improving spatial coverage, and limiting unnecessary energy consumption during underwater recovery operations. This study proposes a Multi-Objective Dhole Optimization Algorithm (MO-DOA) for discrete saturation-aware allocation. Methods: The method maps each candidate to a continuous latent score matrix, decodes it to UUV-to-region assignments, repairs assignment and saturation violations, and uses Pareto dominance with a diversity-preserving external archive to select leaders for the Dhole Optimization Algorithm search, encircling, and attack phases. Results: Evaluation uses an 800 m × 500 m maritime benchmark with eight UUVs, four clustered target regions, and three inaccessible reef zones. In the supplied 20-run results package, MO-DOA attained HV = 0.921, IGD = 0.048, mission effectiveness = 93.8, energy/travel cost = 142.6, threat exposure = 0.220, saturation deviation = 0.50, and runtime = 10.7 s, outperforming CEA, Improved WOA, MDO, IMMP-GWO, and IPSO-VP on the reported criteria. Convergence curves show earlier improvement and sustained Pareto-front quality. Conclusion: The findings support MO-DOA as a compact Pareto-based allocation framework, subject to final verification of the supplied run-level statistics.

title: Did You Hear That? Detecting AI Voice Agents by Exploiting Their Robustness
abstract: AI voice agents enable scalable vishing and impersonation attacks, yet existing detection methods face practical limitations. Artifact-based detectors degrade as synthesis quality improves, challenge–response tests are socially awkward, and adversarial jamming must often be loud or continuous to disrupt modern automatic speech recognition (ASR). We introduce HEARD, a detection framework built on a new principle: instead of perturbing the AI while remaining imperceptible to humans, HEARD applies brief, conspicuous distortions that humans notice but robust ASR systems largely ignore. A human caller is likely to comment on the disturbance, misunderstand the utterance, or request repetition, whereas an AI agent continues coherently from the recovered transcription. We map fifteen audible distortions into three families and evaluate them across six ASR models spanning multiple architectures and five years of development, as well as an experiment involving 41 human volunteers. Using semantic similarity and an LLM-based conversational-legibility metric, we find that across 2,421 LibriSpeech and TED-LIUM utterances, modern ASRs preserve a mean legibility of 97.8%, while the best distortion keeps every model at or above 98.3%. Moreover, performance improves with model recency, making stronger ASR systems easier, not harder, to distinguish from humans.

title: Self-testing of logical subspaces of quantum error-correcting codes
abstract: Abstract We develop explicit device-independent self-testing constructions for logical subspaces of quantum error-correcting codes. By constructing multipartite Bell inequalities tailored to stabilizer code structures, we show that maximal quantum violations uniquely certify that the underlying shared state resides within the logical subspace of a given code, up to local isometries. These constructions extend earlier stabilizer-subspace self-testing results beyond the five-qubit code to several representative stabilizer codes, including the six-qubit code, the Steane code, and Shor's nine-qubit code. The tilted SOS variants further impose algebraic constraints on the relative weights of the logical sectors. Together, these results provide explicit examples of device-independent self-testing for representative stabilizer-code logical subspaces and suggest possible directions for verification and benchmarking of encoded quantum information.

title: Exploring Interpretability in Deep Learning-Based Forest Classification - Separating Similar Forest Classes using Sentinel-2 Time Series
abstract: The ecological insurance theory posits that diverse forests are more resilient and better able to adapt to changing environmental conditions. Increasing drought and heat stress in Central Europe promotes mixed forests for maintaining ecosystem services. However, a diverse species distribution complicates remote sensing-based species mapping, as distinguishing pure from mixed species compositions at the pixel level remains challenging. We evaluated the potential of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for tree-species classification from Sentinel-2 time series and investigated the spectral-temporal features underlying class discrimination, with particular emphasis on separating pure from mixed Norway spruce pixels. We compared RNN classification models with Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and used Integrated Gradients (IG) to quantify feature attributions across spectral bands and time. The best-performing RNN achieved a Macro-F1 score of 0.851 on the test data, outperforming XGBoost by 0.012 and Random Forest by 0.103. Beyond classification performance, the attribution analysis revealed distinct spectral-temporal patterns associated with the separation of pure and mixed Norway spruce pixels. Attribution values increased particularly after approximately day of year (DOY) 125, while B11 showed the strongest contribution during periods of increasing spectral divergence between the two classes. These findings show that recurrent models can provide competitive classification performance while also revealing the phenological periods and spectral regions that are most relevant for distinguishing closely related forest compositions. Combining time-series classification with explainability therefore provides additional insight into the spectral-temporal mechanisms underlying tree-species discrimination and may support more detailed mapping of mixed forest structures.

title: Optimization for One, Feasibility for Most: Decoupling Optimization from Feasibility in Chance-Constrained Programs
abstract: Chance-constrained stochastic programs (CCSPs) require solutions that satisfy uncertain constraints with high probability. Standard approaches either embed scenarios directly into optimization by considering sample average approximation (SAA)-based reformulations, growing prohibitively expensive and often failing to find feasible solutions; or employ conservative reformulations that guarantee feasibility but sacrifice objective quality by design. We propose ACCESS (Adaptive Chance-Constrained Exploration via Structured Sampling), a structured sampling framework that decouples optimization from feasibility evaluation. First, high-quality candidate solutions are generated by solving many inexpensive single-scenario subproblems, avoiding sampling directly in the constrained high-dimensional solution space. Second, feasibility is assessed separately via large-scale batched simulation over a massive number of scenarios, which is naturally amenable to GPU parallelism. That reduces the search from a high-dimensional solution space to a two-dimensional parameter space controlling conservatism and scenario diversity; while concentrating on candidates near the feasibility boundary, where high-quality feasible solutions lie. We also introduce a variant, ACCESS($δ$), which provides certified feasibility guarantees with probability $1-δ$. Experiments across three benchmark classes and five scenario distributions show that ACCESS matches or exceeds the best objective found by any method in nearly every setting, while ACCESS($δ$) is empirically feasible on every instance. The conservative reformulations remain several percent worse in objective, and SAA is frequently infeasible while taking an order of magnitude longer on the harder benchmarks.

title: Perception Beyond the Visible: Incompleteness-Aware Scene Understanding for Robot Autonomy
abstract: Reliable robot autonomy requires reasoning about the world from partial and noisy observations. However, many perception systems model only visible scene regions, rely on fixed semantic categories, and assume reliable sensor measurements. These assumptions break under occlusion, novel object encounters, and sensor degradation. In this paper, I present a research vision for incompleteness-aware scene understanding. I organize this vision around three fundamental challenges: incomplete evidence, incomplete knowledge, and incomplete sensor reliability. I discuss my research contributions toward addressing these challenges through amodal perception, semantic occupancy forecasting, open-world scene understanding, label-efficient learning, and uncertainty-guided multi-modal fusion. Building on these contributions, I outline future research directions toward belief-centric 4D scene representations. These representations aim to jointly model geometry, semantics, motion, and uncertainty. I also discuss active sensing and safe adaptation strategies that allow robots to reduce uncertainty through interaction. The goal is to develop calibrated and actionable scene representations that support reliable autonomy in dynamic, open-world environments.

title: VARI: Robust Text-to-Video Generation via Group-Structured Intent Alignment
abstract: Modern text-to-video (T2V) models generate visually compelling videos, yet meaning-preserving changes in prompt wording can substantially alter semantic realization and overall quality. Existing prompt rewriting modifies the inference input, whereas conventional post-training constructs supervision from one prompt formulation at a time; neither explicitly optimizes reliability across equivalent forms. We introduce VARI (Verified Alignment over Representations of Intent), a group-structured framework that treats automatically verified formulations of the same visual intent as a shared supervision unit. VARI builds matched form-seed rollout pools, cross-scores each video against all forms, and applies a wording-independent structured intent audit to identify valid realizations and hard semantic failures. Group-Consistent Distillation (GCD) aligns every verified form with interchangeable valid realizations, while Form-Contrastive Flow-DPO (FC-DPO) learns group-level preferences from audited positive-negative pairs, prioritizing same-seed, different-form contrasts. On HunyuanVideo-1.5, VARI attains the highest T2V-CompBench, VBench, and StoryEval scores among the evaluated methods. On prompt-form extensions of T2V-CompBench and VBench, it improves weakest-form alignment over the strongest prompt-level baselines by 2.45 and 3.55 points and reduces cross-form drop by 30.5% and 32.2%, respectively, while preserving visual quality. Human evaluation, natural-caption controls, prompt-enhancement experiments, diversity analyses, and transfer to LTX-2.3 further support the robustness and transferability of these gains, while VARI requires no additional inference-time module.

title: How to Train Your Intercept: A Comparison of Intercept Update Strategies in Coordinate Descent
abstract: Coordinate descent solvers for regularized generalized linear models (GLMs) differ in how they update the intercept. This seemingly routine choice can substantially affect convergence when the response is imbalanced. For direct coordinate descent on the original GLM loss, we compare a conservative step based on worst-case curvature, a safeguarded Newton step based on current curvature, and repeated Newton steps that solve the intercept subproblem. The conservative update can leave much of the interaction between the intercept and the coefficients unresolved, producing a slowdown when that interaction controls convergence. A single Newton step avoids this attenuation and, in our experiments, follows nearly the same outer trajectory as exact minimization while requiring fewer inner steps. Simulated and real-data experiments, including comparisons across six production solvers and a controlled intervention within skglm, support this explanation. We also show how the same mechanism appears in quadratic-approximation methods and extends to multinomial models with rare classes. We recommend a safeguarded Newton update for direct coordinate descent and full intercept optimization within frozen local quadratic surrogates.

title: AI-Enhanced Hyperspectral Imaging for Intraoperative Detection of Low-Grade Glioma: A Clinical Study
abstract: Current image-guided neuronavigation techniques, such as intraoperative MRI and ultrasound, are limited by high costs, limited sensitivity and operational complexity. There is a clear need for more efficient systems to enhance intra-operative tumor detection and improve patient outcomes for intrinsic brain tumor resection. Whereas previous intraoperative brain HSI studies have predominantly investigated high-grade gliomas, glioblastomas, or mixed-grade cohorts, this clinical study focuses specifically on low-grade gliomas (LGGs). LGGs strongly resemble normal brain under white light conditions on the operative microscope. This study characterizes spectral differences between healthy and tumor tissue and provides a paired comparison of HSI- and RGB-based classification at matched tissue locations and under identical patient-level data splits. Tumor regions showed consistently lower reflectance, which may be associated with differences in hemoglobin concentration and oxygenation. A range of classification models was evaluated. The 3D CNN, which integrates spectral and spatial features, achieved the highest median ROC-AUC of 74.5%, compared with 67.9% for the spectral-only XGBoost model and 64.0% for the RGB-based model. These results support further investigation of HSI for low-grade glioma classification and quantify its performance relative to conventional RGB imaging in this cohort.

title: Importancia de la inteligencia artificial en el éxito de los emprendimientos
abstract: La inteligencia artificial (IA) se ha convertido en la herramienta número uno en excelencia tanto para jóvenes como para adultos dentro del entorno empresarial y no solo eso si no la vida en general, debido a su capacidad para transformar procesos, optimizar recursos y generar nuevas oportunidades de innovación. En el contexto de los emprendimientos, empieza a tomar mucha relevancia pues la incorporación de soluciones basadas en inteligencia artificial representa una alternativa estratégica e indispensable para mejorar la productividad, fortalecer la toma de decisiones y aumentar la competitividad en mercados cada vez más dinámicos y exigentes nivel global. El presente trabajo tiene como objetivo principal analizar la importancia de la inteligencia artificial en los emprendimientos, identificando y analizando sus principales aplicaciones, beneficios y desafíos para contribuir al éxito, desarrollo y sostenibilidad empresarial en plena era de expansión. Por esto se desarrolla una investigación de tipo documental basada en la revisión y análisis de fuentes académicas, artículos científicos, informes especializados y documentos relacionados con la inteligencia artificial, la innovación empresarial y el emprendimiento. Los resultados presentados del análisis permiten evidenciar que la inteligencia artificial ofrece múltiples ventajas para los nuevos negocios y no solo eso también presenta una herramienta en ciertos puntos confiables para micronegocios y emprendimientos emergentes, entre ellas la automatización de actividades se presenta como la parte mas fundamental a la hora de mirar el impacto presente en estas nueva era, siempre y cuando los emprendedores cuenten con la preparación necesaria para utilizarla como una herramienta estratégica de desarrollo.

title: SBR-4 Adaptive Adversary Battery — No Structural Gradient Exists; the Conforming-Injection Boundary Quantified (FS-A5 Ships as Found)
abstract: Adaptive-adversary battery: a bandit-style adaptive attacker probed the ingestion guard across the full input space. Bandit telemetry across the run shows ZERO structural wins — no exploitable gradient exists for an adaptive attacker to climb. 42 heals were correctly attributed to attacker-injected traffic (accounted as attacker contributions, not silent acceptance); 1 collateral decision flip was disclosed and traced. Five instrument defects were disclosed between runs; a proposed goalpost narrowing was REJECTED (the prereg bar stood as frozen). The conforming-injection boundary is quantified: FS-A5 ships as found, with SIP-2/SIP-3 evidence attached. Operator authorization: Leon GO (chat authorization, 11:55 CT, Oct 13, 2026). Scope honesty: single-run preregistered falsifier battery on synthetic data against a prototype governed self-healing system; no production claim is made or implied. Operator authorization recorded as GO + timestamp per the operator-privacy doctrine. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects on them.

title: What should a knowledge-tracing model remember? Evidence from Chemistry
abstract: Digital learning environments provide extensive longitudinal records of student performance, but it is unclear how much of this history is useful for predicting subsequent responses. This study examined predictive compression in 1,975,329 chemistry responses from 4,591 Finnish students in Grades 7–9, evaluated on held-out students. An item-only model achieved an AUC of .7566. Compressing response history into a single recency-weighted scalar increased AUC to .8119, while a 128-dimensional single-summary transformer performed similarly (.8112). Nested target-independent states improved gradually with dimensionality, reaching an AUC of .8242 at 750 dimensions, with performance still improving at the upper end of the tested range.In contrast, a query-conditioned transformer, allowing the target item to attend selectively to previous responses, achieved .8519. Thus, much of the predictive information in student histories was highly compressible, but substantial additional information depended on target-specific access to history. The results show that it matters not only how much information a model keeps about a student, but also how it uses that information.

title: Controlled Evaluation of Document-Level Inter-Mention Links for Named-Entity Type Classification in Ukrainian Texts
abstract: Document-level links between repeated mentions can provide contextual evidence unavailable to a local entity-type classifier, a potentially important capability for Ukrainian because of its limited annotated resources and rich inflectional morphology. However, their specific contribution is difficult to isolate because graph-based systems often simultaneously alter the classifier architecture. We evaluate named-entity type classification with known mention boundaries on NER-UK 2.0 under controlled conditions, using frozen XLM-RoBERTa-base representations, 10 optimization seeds, and 270 graph-head training runs. The evaluation design combines a no-message baseline with matched head parameterization, degree-preserving topology shuffling, simple averaging, oracle diagnostics, and controlled context-weakening interventions; no novel graph architecture is claimed. On intervention-free data, the exact-repeat graph changed macro-F1 by +0.0041 (95% CI [−0.0042,0.0127]); thus, an overall benefit was not established, although the interval did not rule out a practically meaningful effect. A Ukrainian token-level lemmatization rule increased graph coverage from 34.41% to 42.07% but did not improve performance over exact repetition (Δ=−0.0033, 95% CI [−0.0135,0.0055]). When only the target mention’s context was artificially weakened, with no explicit degradation cue, graph refinement increased target accuracy by 0.0784 (95% CI [0.0544,0.1021]). The advantage reversed when the entire repeat component was weakened, while simple averaging performed at least as well as the learned graph head. Overall, the results support graph-based refinement as a conditional context-recovery mechanism rather than a universal replacement for local classification. The evidence remains controlled but not independently confirmatory and does not establish gains for end-to-end NER or robustness to naturally degraded context.

title: Blockchain-enabled privacy and trust in federated learning architectures
abstract: Data has become as valuable as crude oil, powering innovative projects and transformative systems across industries. However, the standard machine learning approach often falls flat in protecting sensitive information from exposure because it relies on centralized computing for model training. In order to reduce risks, a distributed methodology known as federated learning was developed. Federated learning qualifies collaborative model training without migrating raw data to a central server, thereby preserving client privacy. In spite of that, federated learning cannot pledge security, verifiability, or coordination within its ecosystem. Meanwhile, blockchain technology has emerged as a cornerstone for the next generation of the internet (Web3.0), allowing users to gain greater authority over their data through a decentralized architecture and encouraging a shift from traditional centralized systems to a more modern approach. The combination of cooperative intelligence (federated learning) with blockchain technology will open the doors to a new era in artificial intelligence. The fusion of these two powers is a gateway to the building of reshaping systems that will shift entire industries. In this chapter, our focus will be on exploring federated learning as a novel learning pattern and studying the effectiveness of its integration with blockchain to ensure security, trustworthiness, and transparency, as well as providing an overview of current research in this area.

title: Universal Hamiltonian control in a planar trimon circuit
abstract: Multimode circuits provide an avenue for flexible control of single and multi-qubit gates. In this work we implement a multimode circuit known as a trimon integrated in a planar geometry. The trimon features three transmon-like modes with strong all-to-all $ZZ$ coupling. We demonstrate high fidelity operations on the trimon, achieving flexible control of its rich state space. This includes qubit rotations conditioned on one or both other qubits, unconditional single-qubit rotations, and both excitation-conserving and double-excitation two-qubit entangling gates. Through multi-tone driving we are able to implement all 16 two-qubit Pauli operators in the two-qubit space. We further demonstrate using the trimon as a qudit with up to 8 states and higher coherence than typical transmon-based implementations. Our results show a compact, highly controllable device that can potentially replace transmons in standard superconducting processor architectures.

title: An iterative knowledge extraction and dual-channel fusion framework for clinical differential diagnosis
abstract: For common diseases in the cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and respiratory systems that present with overlapping clinical manifestations (for instance, chest tightness and shortness of breath), accurate identification is critical for formulating effective treatment plans. However, the unstructured nature of medical records and the implicit relationships embedded in medical knowledge pose significant challenges to automated diagnosis. Existing methods overlook medical commonsense and triplet relational structures, rendering them incapable of capturing symptom–disease associations and consequently limiting their discriminative ability for diseases with similar clinical presentations. To address these limitations, we construct the Chinese Clinical Document–Electronic Medical Record (CCD-EMR) dataset for complex common diseases and propose the Knowledge-enhanced Iterative Diagnostic Framework (KIDF). This model achieves in-depth analysis of complex clinical phenotypes through a knowledge extraction–dual-channel fusion mechanism. Specifically, the medical knowledge triplet extraction module combines large language models with a rule-based knowledge base to extract high-fidelity structured knowledge from free-text medical records. The dual-channel fusion module integrates BERT and TransE to fuse medical record semantics with graph embeddings, which are subsequently refined by a hybrid feature classifier to accurately capture local key patterns and long-range semantic dependencies. Experimental results demonstrate that the KIDF model achieves 77.19% accuracy and a 62.94% macro-average F1 score on the CCD-EMR dataset. Ablation studies further confirm that the proposed modules play a crucial role in enhancing diagnostic performance for complex common diseases.

title: Known-Voice Cloning and the Limits of Personality Transfer for Character Design
abstract: Recent advances in zero-shot voice cloning systems make it possible to reproduce a recognizable voice from a short recording and attach it to arbitrary virtual characters. Prior work suggests that familiar vocal identity can carry over associated personality impressions to new targets such as robots or virtual characters. However, these works have mainly examined familiarity and personalization effects rather than directly testing whether a cloned familiar voice systematically transfers personality impressions to an embodied virtual character. Such transference raises the concern that cloned voices could be used to manipulate people into engaging with virtual characters as capable social actors. Across two studies, we investigated whether personality impressions transfer when a virtual character speaks with the cloned voice of a familiar person. Study 1 examined this question in a real-world university setting using the cloned voice of a lecturer familiar to the participating students. Study 2 examined the same question online using voices of social media content creators and members of their communities. Drawing on the concepts of identity activation, trait transfer, and person reconstruction, we show that evidence of personality transfer was limited in both studies. Observed effects were selective and did not generalize across traits or study contexts. In the online study in particular, recognizable voice identity cues activated expectations about the speaker but did not reconstruct the broader person impression. Qualitative responses further indicated that judgments were frequently shaped by perceived artificiality and by whether voice and appearance fit together. Our findings moderate common concerns that cloned voices straightforwardly manipulate people into perceiving artificial characters as capable social actors.

title: Sea-Net: A Small and Inherently Interpretable Neural Network for Time Series Classification
abstract: Traditional time-series classification methods often operate as black boxes, providing a class prediction without indicating which time point or time interval within the series led to that prediction. To improve temporal interpretability, MILLET (Multiple Instance Learning with Temporal Explanation), which combines an InceptionTime encoder with Conjunctive Pooling, provides both classification and temporal explanations. However, MILLET contains approximately 424 K parameters, making it unsuitable for deployment on resource-constrained micro-controllers, and it achieves an overall time-series accuracy of 0.888 and an explanation score of 0.681 NDCG@n. We therefore propose SEA-Net, a lightweight architecture using small multi-scale depthwise-separable convolutional TSC encoders and improved Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) pooling heads. Our SEA-Net bottleneck encoder with Top-k pooling achieves 0.931 accuracy and 0.765 NDCG@n with only 41 K parameters. Another variant, using a gated encoder with Top-k pooling, achieves 0.955 accuracy and 0.750 NDCG@n with 62 K parameters. These results demonstrate that lightweight architectures can maintain strong classification performance and temporal explanations while substantially reducing model size. The proposed variants address specific limitations of the pooling strategy used by MILLET, providing a practical direction for interpretable time-series classification on resource-constrained edge devices.

title: ECG-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Targeted Electrocardiogram Waveform Evolution
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) models need supervision that targets evolving weaknesses and remains faithful to waveform evidence. We introduce ECG-RSI, a recursive self-improvement framework combining verified waveform synthesis with feedback-guided intervention search. Signal remeasurement verifies waveform edits; construction errors guide generator repair, while learner errors motivate interventions compared on a separate selection set. Across seven benchmarks, three rounds raise Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's mean question-answering accuracy from 34.57% to 56.04% and mean classification F1 from 24.27 to 34.03. Across the retained trajectory, the preferred supervision shifts from direct reinforcement to confusion-focused contrasts. Continued feedback correction yields diminishing external gains. These results motivate separating error diagnosis from intervention selection and checking whether gains on the feedback set transfer to independent benchmarks.

title: POLVIZX: un prototipo multiplataforma para la construcción y la exploración de árboles de posturas
abstract: Opinion polarization in social media challenges public discourse and informed decision-making. POLVIZ, a prior web prototype, analyzed polarized opinions through stance detection, topic modeling, argument synthesis, and visual analytics. This paper presents POLVIZX, a cross-platform extension offering both desktop web and mobile applications for exploring polarized opinion spaces on any dataset. POLVIZX organizes opinions into hierarchical stance trees, grouping arguments by topic and stance (pro/anti), to help users navigate debates and identify polarization patterns, with a pipeline supporting partial execution and reuse of intermediate results for iterative analysis. Each application offers interaction and visualization strategies suited to its platform, while Firebase-based authentication enables cross-device synchronization, stance tree sharing, and collaborative exploration. This extension broadens access to opinion polarization tools and supports emerging e-deliberation scenarios.

title: Implementasi Hybrid Algortima RSA dan Vernam Cipher Menggunakan Model DevSecOps untuk Keamanan Data Pegawai pada BPKPAD Kabupaten Balangan
abstract: Keamanan data pegawai merupakan aspek penting dalam menjaga kerahasiaan informasi pada instansi pemerintah. Pengelolaan data secara digital tanpa mekanisme pengamanan yang memadai berpotensi menimbulkan akses tidak sah, kebocoran data, serta penyalahgunaan informasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengimplementasikan hybrid algoritma RSA dan Vernam Cipher menggunakan model DevSecOps untuk meningkatkan keamanan data pegawai pada Badan Pengelolaan Keuangan, Pendapatan, dan Aset Daerah (BPKPAD) Kabupaten Balangan. Metode penelitian meliputi identifikasi kebutuhan sistem, perancangan aplikasi berbasis web menggunakan framework Laravel 11, implementasi algoritma hybrid untuk proses enkripsi dan dekripsi file, penerapan prinsip DevSecOps melalui mekanisme logging aktivitas, serta pengujian sistem menggunakan Black Box Testing, White Box Testing, pengujian waktu proses, dan evaluasi keamanan sistem. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sistem mampu melakukan proses enkripsi dan dekripsi file secara konsisten sehingga dokumen yang telah dienkripsi tidak dapat diakses tanpa mekanisme autentikasi dan kunci yang sesuai. Implementasi DevSecOps juga mendukung proses pemantauan aktivitas pengguna melalui pencatatan log sehingga meningkatkan kemampuan audit dan pengawasan keamanan sistem. Dengan demikian, penerapan hybrid algoritma RSA dan Vernam Cipher yang dipadukan dengan model DevSecOps mampu meningkatkan perlindungan data pegawai secara lebih aman, terintegrasi, dan terkelola pada lingkungan BPKPAD Kabupaten Balangan

title: Geometry vs Binary: Quantum Physics Puzzles — quantum geometry problem unsolved by machine learn — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: ## Binary Failure → Geometry Solution **Analysis of Findings:** The search results reveal a critical gap: quantum machine learning (QML) researchers are *borrowing* geometric ideas (e.g., Cerezo's "Geometric Quantum Machine Learning") but still framing them as **optimization problems over parameter spaces** — a fundamentally statistical approach. title: An independent certified computation excluding four mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
abstract: We show that there are no four mutually unbiased bases in ℂ⁶, so that the maximum number of such bases is three. The proof is computer-assisted and assumes that the machine on which the computation ran carried out binary64 arithmetic correctly, as made precise in Section 3.1. It carries out the discretization proof of a recent preprint by OpenAI, which has not appeared in a refereed journal. Our programs are written from the text of the preprint, and we prove every statement of the preprint that our proof uses. Four mutually unbiased bases could be taken to consist of the standard basis, the columns of a complex Hadamard matrix divided by √6, and two further bases. Finitely many balls in phase coordinates cover all complex Hadamard matrices of order six up to equivalence, and on each small ball a finite search shows that these two further bases do not exist. Every inequality that the programs decide in order to reject a case or to cover a set of matrices is decided in exact integer arithmetic or in interval arithmetic with outward rounding. The programs, with the logs and data of the computation, are deposited.

title: HistoBreastCAD: an integrated deep learning framework for segmentation and multiclass classification of whole-slide breast histopathology images
abstract: Breast cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, and histopathological examination remains the diagnostic gold standard. This study presents HistoBreastCAD, an integrated deep learning framework that combines tissue-region segmentation, four-class histopathology classification, spatial mapping of predictions, and interactive whole-slide image (WSI) review. Segmentation was evaluated using WSI-grouped five-fold cross-validation, while classification used source-image-grouped five-fold cross-validation to prevent source-level data leakage. The final DeepLabV3+ L0 segmentation configuration achieved an out-of-fold micro-Dice of 0.8390 , IoU of 0.7226 , precision of 0.8278 , and recall of 0.8505 . For classification, EfficientNetB0 was the strongest individual model, while a frozen equal-weight soft-voting ensemble of EfficientNetB0 and ResNet18-GAP-attention achieved an accuracy of 0.8283 ± 0.0320 and macro-F1 of 0.8282 ± 0.0316 , outperforming EfficientNetB0 in all five validation folds. An exploratory reader study using the 100 microscopy images from the held-out BACH test set showed moderate interobserver agreement between two pathologists (Cohen’s κ = 0.5105; n = 95), whereas model-to-reader concordance was lower. The ensemble did not increase reader concordance relative to EfficientNetB0. HistoBreastCAD therefore demonstrates the feasibility of integrating established deep learning components into a source-separated WSI-oriented digital pathology workflow. However, external multi-institutional validation, adjudicated reader studies, and formal explainability assessment are required before claims of clinical generalizability or utility can be supported.

title: CCD-MAF: A Cognitive Conceptualization Diagram-driven Multi-Agent Framework for structured CBT dialogue generation
abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown potential in mental health support, existing approaches often provide unstructured emotional responses and struggle to deliver structured, evidence-based interventions such as Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT). Existing CBT dialogue datasets also lack sufficient clinical depth and phase-specific patient resistance. To address these limitations, we construct the CCD-CBT Dataset, a multi-phase CBT dialogue corpus integrating expert textbook knowledge with real-world doctor–patient interactions sourced from Haodf Online and other medical consultation websites. The dataset contains 1314 samples covering the four standard CBT treatment phases, from initial assessment to termination, with an average dialogue length of 132.12 turns. The average utterance length is 61.34 Chinese characters for patients and 97.05 Chinese characters for therapists. Based on this dataset, we propose CCD-MAF, a hierarchical Multi-Agent Framework guided by the Cognitive Conceptualization Diagram (CCD). CCD-MAF decomposes the CBT counseling process into macro-phase planning, meso-state tracking, and micro-technique execution, enabling dynamic modeling of patients’ cognitive structures and targeted interventions. We fine-tune Qwen2.5-7B as the therapist component within CCD-MAF and conduct single-turn and multi-turn clinical simulations. The evaluation distinguishes system-level comparisons among independently operated systems from therapist-component substitution comparisons within the shared CCD-MAF framework. Results indicate that CCD-MAF demonstrates strong performance in Cognitive Therapy Scale (CTS)-based simulated evaluations. In the component-substitution setting, the fine-tuned therapist component achieves the best performance among the evaluated therapist components under the same CCD-MAF framework. Ablation studies further support the contribution of the proposed multi-agent mechanism. This study provides an interpretable and clinically structured framework for developing AI psychological assistants, with its effectiveness evaluated in simulated counseling settings.

title: MemeTrace: A Multimodal LLM-Based Agent for Safety-Aware Meme Provenance Analysis
abstract: Online memes are often carriers of unsafe content such as disinformation and propaganda. Their rapid evolution in response to news events and strong dependence on contextual information make it difficult for platforms and moderators to detect and moderate them effectively. Moreover, existing moderation studies typically classify memes as safe or unsafe based on individual images, lacking the ability to perform broader provenance analysis, i.e., where a meme originates, how it spreads, what cultural symbolism it represents, whether it poses potential risks to society, etc. To bridge this gap, we introduce MemeTrace, a multimodal LLM-based agent that automatically traces the provenance and potential risks of emerging memes. We evaluate MemeTrace on Meme100, a dataset of 100 real-world memes, using both human annotation and automatic metrics. The results demonstrate that MemeTrace substantially outperforms the VLM baseline. More importantly, MemeTrace achieves higher accuracy in detecting unsafe memes, especially those involving disinformation and sensitive content, and remains robust under visual perturbations.

title: How Far Can Coding Agents Go in Visual Generation?
abstract: Modern image generation largely relies on specialized generative models that leave the process of image construction implicit in learned parameters. We explore an alternative: general-purpose coding agents that construct images through executable programs. Our study of zero-shot drawing on AgentDrawBench, a 200-prompt benchmark, reveals a distinctive capability profile. Agents excel at preserving structure and satisfying precise visual constraints, achieving competitive results in domains where compositional accuracy matters more than photorealistic appearance, while remaining limited in perceptual richness. Their visual expressiveness varies with the drawing interface, and a qualitative study on reconstruction shows how procedural skills extracted from human demonstrations support different artistic media. We then examine code as an external visual language of thought: a structured, executable representation that agents can construct and inspect. We test it in visual question answering task and find reconstructed visual code retains substantial information for question answering and, in some domains, supports higher accuracy than the original image. These abilities raise a further question: do agents draw on a shared internal representation of scene content beyond a particular drawing program? We explore an internal visual language-of-thought hypothesis, in which a shared, compositionally structured representation supports visual operations across drawing languages. Cross-harness drawings and images assembled from independent single-pixel queries exhibit related layouts and tones. Agents also maintain self-generated room arrangements across viewpoints after visible drawings are removed. These results demonstrate that the coding agent would maintain a consistent and coherent world inside its imagine even before the harness gets involved and the generation starts.

title: $\mathrm{S}^3$-PnP: Plug-and-Play Denoising for Scientific Imaging with Self-Supervised Score Priors
abstract: Modern image restoration methods increasingly rely on large-scale supervised training, yet clean targets are often prohibitively difficult to obtain in scientific imaging modalities such as hyperspectral imaging (HSI) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Plug-and-play ADMM (PnP-ADMM) with pretrained diffusion priors offers a promising alternative, but the learned prior distribution can mismatch both the target scientific image distribution and the distribution of ADMM denoiser inputs induced by dual feedback. To mitigate these mismatches, we propose $\mathrm{S}^3$-PnP, a self-supervised plug-and-play restoration framework that learns a score prior directly from observation-derived ADMM intermediate states, without clean training targets or externally pretrained weights. Specifically, the learned score corrects the input to the analytical prior update, combining observation-driven corrections with analytical regularization. We further analyze the convergence and reconstruction error of the corrected ADMM algorithm assuming an ideal score and quadratic data fidelity. Experiments on reference-guided HSI restoration, single-image HSI denoising, and MRI denoising demonstrate consistent improvements over competing methods.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Large-Scale Lifelong Multi-Agent Path Finding with Shared Spatial Fields
abstract: Large-scale applications of lifelong multi-agent path finding (LMAPF) call for computationally inexpensive movement decisions under changing traffic conditions and across varied layouts. We propose a navigation policy in which a convolutional network computes a shared spatial field over the map once per timestep and a compact goal-conditioned operator derives agents' movement preferences. The complete policy is trained end-to-end using average-reward reinforcement learning with throughput as the reward, without planner demonstrations or a separate online path planner. For structured and unstructured layouts, we train one policy per class on mixtures of small maps and deploy each without retraining on larger, unseen layouts and agent populations. Across six layouts with 10000 agents, our policies achieve throughput comparable to or higher than the strongest evaluated baselines. The proposed method has an average execution time below 10 ms per step, more than an order of magnitude faster than several established planners.

title: MERIT: Multimodal Evidence Reasoning over Image Tables
abstract: Table reasoning with language models typically assumes access to clean textual tables. In practice, tables are often serialized into text, which can corrupt cell contents, distort structural relationships, and discard visual cues, leaving the model to reason over incomplete evidence. In contrast, table images retain this information, but using it requires both accurate perception and reasoning grounded in the relevant cells. To address this, we propose MERIT (Multimodal Evidence Reasoning over Image Tables), a three-stage framework for learning to reason over table images, with serialized tables serving as optional auxiliary inputs (if provided). Our analysis identifies visual evidence acquisition as a bottleneck, motivating table-specific encoder adaptation through reconstruction, localization, and color-conditioned supervision. Building on the adapted representations, supervised fine-tuning teaches explicit evidence selection and reasoning using verified trajectories. Finally, reinforcement learning refines the policy with separate rewards for evidence correctness, calculation, final answers, and output format. By providing feedback on intermediate steps, the framework targets retrieval and computational errors that final-answer supervision alone does not distinguish. We evaluate the approach on table question answering and fact verification, analyze the contributions of visual inputs and training components, and assess generalization to additional datasets with different table structures and visual presentations.

title: MissPath-FM: Flow Matching with Structured Priors for Partially Observed Time Series
abstract: Flow matching has emerged as a powerful alternative to diffusion models for generative modeling, but standard conditional flow matching is fundamentally misaligned with partially observed time series: starting from an uninformed Gaussian source forces the model to transport even already-observed entries from noise to the target, wasting capacity on trivially known regions. We propose MissPath-FM, a partial-observation-aware flow matching framework that redesigns the source prior and probability path for incomplete time series. MissPath-FM employs structured source priors (interpolation priors and Gaussian process posterior priors) to initialize the flow close to the observed signal, paired with a missingness-aware smooth path that allocates transport asymmetrically between observed and missing regions. We evaluate systematically across four datasets, four missingness mechanisms (MCAR, block, MNAR, irregular), two missing ratios, and three sequence lengths (T in {24, 48, 96}), totaling 48 settings against eight baselines. MissPath-FM wins 29 of 32 settings at T=48 and 45 of 48 overall (93.8%). Our ablations reveal a regime-dependent design hierarchy in which no single component suffices: under random missingness the source prior yields a large initial gain, but under structured block missingness it can fail entirely and the learned flow becomes indispensable; the missingness-aware path contributes a further 12%-26% across all regimes. Mechanistically, structured priors shorten observed-region transport by up to 15x, concentrating the velocity field on genuinely uncertain entries. Our ablations reveal a regime-dependent design hierarchy in which no single component suffices: under random missingness the source prior yields a large initial gain, but under structured block missingness it can fail entirely and the learned flow becomes indispensable; the missingness-aware path contributes a further 12%-26% across all regimes. Mechanistically, structured priors shorten observed-region transport by up to 15x, concentrating the velocity field on genuinely uncertain entries. title: Towards studying superconductivity in the Fermi-Hubbard model on Rydberg atoms
abstract: Abstract We present a method for calculating the ground state energy of the Fermi-Hubbard model leveraging Rydberg atom processors and sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD). By exploiting the perturbative relationship between the Fermi-Hubbard and Heisenberg models, the procedure samples from the Heisenberg model as prepared on the Rydberg atom processor, and uses the samples to diagonalize the Fermi-Hubbard model for large U . We include anisotropy and next-nearest-neighbor interactions and discuss the relevant regime for quasi-superconductivity in the 1-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model. Numerical and experimental results on the Aquila quantum processor are presented for ground state energy calculations as well as the chemical potential. We find that the Heisenberg model sampling in the studied regime is sufficient to converge near to the ground state for up to 56 qubits, and we see a clear advantage of Rydberg atom sampling as opposed to random sampling even with 10 times more samples for diagonalization. We also present a gate-based implementation of the gate-based SQD algorithm on IBM Quantum hardware for 56-qubit Hubbard model as a benchmark. Finally, we provide a gap analysis for studying emergent superconductivity using this method.

title: Neural network ensembles for mitigating uncertainty in classification tasks
abstract: Η αναγνώριση οδηγικής συμπεριφοράς από δεδομένα αισθητήρων οχήματος αποτελεί σημαντικό πρόβλημα ταξινόμησης πολυμεταβλητών χρονοσειρών, με εφαρμογές στην ασφάλεια οδήγησης, την εξατομίκευση συστημάτων οχήματος και την ανίχνευση μη εξουσιοδοτημένης χρήσης. Η εφαρμογή σύγχρονων transformer-based αρχιτεκτονικών σε τέτοια προβλήματα παραμένει προκλητική όταν ο διαθέσιμος όγκος δεδομένων είναι περιορισμένος καθώς τα μοντέλα αυτά τείνουν να υπερπροσαρμόζονται και να παρουσιάζουν ασταθή επίδοση. Η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία διερευνά κατά πόσο ο συνδυασμός πολλαπλών εξειδικευμένων μοντέλων μέσω ensemble μεθόδων μπορεί να μετριάσει αυτούς τους περιορισμούς. Χρησιμοποιώντας το δημόσιο σύνολο δεδομένων HCRL Driving Dataset (10 οδηγοί, 54 κανάλια αισθητήρων), το πρόβλημα των δέκα οδηγών χωρίστηκε σε τρεις μικρότερες, μη επικαλυπτόμενες ομάδες και εκπαιδεύτηκε ανεξάρτητα ένα μοντέλο ConvTran σε κάθε ομάδα. Τα τρία εκπαιδευμένα μοντέλα χρησιμοποιήθηκαν στη συνέχεια αποκλειστικά ως εξαγωγείς χαρακτηριστικών: οι ενδιάμεσες αναπαραστάσεις (embeddings) που παρήγαγαν για δεδομένα και των δέκα οδηγών συνδυάστηκαν σε ένα ενιαίο διάνυσμα, πάνω στο οποίο εκπαιδεύτηκε τελικός ταξινομητής Random Forest. Για την αξιολόγηση της συνεισφοράς της μεθόδου, η επίδοση του ensemble συστήματος συγκρίθηκε στο ίδιο ανεξάρτητο σύνολο ελέγχου, με δύο εναλλακτικές προσεγγίσεις: έναν ταξινομητή Random Forest πάνω σε στατιστικά χαρακτηριστικά ακατέργαστων δεδομένων, και ένα μεμονωμένο ConvTran εκπαιδευμένο απευθείας στο πλήρες πρόβλημα, χωρίς καμία μορφή ensemble.Το προτεινόμενο σύστημα πέτυχε ακρίβεια 67.24%, υπερτερώντας και των δύο εναλλακτικών (55.30% και 53.95% αντίστοιχα), αναδεικνύοντας τη δυνατότητα του συνδυασμού εξειδικευμένων αναπαραστάσεων να βελτιώνει την ταξινόμηση. Παράλληλα, η εργασία αναδεικνύει σημαντικές μεθοδολογικές προκλήσεις κατά την εφαρμογή Deep Learning σε μικρά σύνολα δεδομένων χρονοσειρών, όπως η ευαισθησία στην τυχαία αρχικοποίηση παραμέτρων, και προτείνει πρακτικές αντιμετώπισης τους.

title: Assessing the Robustness of TerraMind to Sensor Domain Gap for On-board Processing on the Φ-sat-2 Mission
abstract: On-board processing is a promising answer to the downlink latency and bandwidth constraints that limit the usefulness of Earth observation data for time-critical applications such as ood and wildre response. Geospatial Foundation Models (GeoFMs) are interesting candidates for this task, since their large-scale multimodal pre-training gives semantic feature extractors that generalize across tasks with few labeled examples. However, these models are pre-trained on archived data from missions such as Sentinel-2, and their behaviour once they are exposed to a new sensor is not known. This thesis studies three questions, with TerraMind, a Vision Transformer (ViT)-based GeoFM, and the European Space Agency's Φ-sat-2 CubeSat mission as the case study: whether TerraMind produces domain-invariant latent representations on real Φ-sat-2 imagery, whether a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) distilled from it can be made sensor-adaptive, and whether doing so is better than simply training the compact model on the target sensor.

title: Robotics-Integrated STEM Education: Fostering Creativity, Innovation and Scientific Inquiry
abstract: Robotics-integrated Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) education offers opportunities to connect theoretical knowledge with practical problem-solving, creative design, and scientific investigation. By designing, constructing, programming, and testing robotic systems, learners can explore scientific principles, apply mathematical reasoning, develop technological skills, and evaluate engineering solutions. This thematic article examines how robotics-integrated STEM education can foster creativity, innovation, and scientific inquiry, while considering the teaching approaches and institutional conditions that influence its educational value. The discussion draws on published systematic reviews and meta-analyses, alongside established perspectives on constructionist learning, inquiry-based education, and engineering design. Existing evidence suggests that educational robotics can support STEM learning and creativity, although outcomes vary according to learners’ age, instructional design, subject area, duration, and teacher support. Robotics activities are most educationally meaningful when learners investigate authentic problems, generate and compare alternative solutions, test prototypes, interpret evidence, and revise their designs. However, equipment costs, unequal access, insufficient teacher preparation, excessive emphasis on coding, and limited assessment of creative and scientific processes may restrict the benefits. The article argues that robotics should be integrated into STEM curricula as a means of inquiry and design rather than treated merely as a technical activity. It proposes a pedagogical framework linking problem identification, scientific investigation, creative design, prototype testing, evidence-based revision, and reflection. The article concludes that the educational value of robotics depends less on the presence of robotic equipment than on the quality of the learning experiences developed around it.

title: Machine-Readable No-Learn Protocols and Fiduciary Governance Under the Extraterritorial Brussels Effect: Technical Specifications, Defensive Publication, and Board Liability Interlocks for Sovereign Intellectual Property
abstract: Abstract: Frontier generative artificial intelligence (AI) developers increasingly engage in regulatory arbitrage, relocating corporate entities to permissive jurisdictions while ingesting public intellectual output via automated web crawling, lossy parameter extraction, and model distillation. However, under Article 2(1)(c) of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), the "Brussels Effect" exerts unavoidable extraterritorial jurisdiction whenever model outputs are utilized within the European single market. Concurrently, Article 53(1)(c) mandates General-Purpose AI (GPAI) providers to respect machine-readable opt-outs under Article 4(3) of the CDSM Directive (Directive (EU) 2019/790). This treatise formalizes a dual-layer technical and statutory defense architecture for independent research sovereignty: (1) The Machine-Readable No-Learn Protocol (NLL-v1.0-2026), integrating cryptographic hashing, persistent digital object identifiers (DOI) anchored on CERN Zenodo, and standardized XMP/HTTP metadata headers that cryptographically signal automated opt-outs, invalidating fair use defenses; (2) Defensive Publication as Prior Art, leveraging immutable Zenodo timestamps to deterministically destroy patent novelty (35 U.S.C. § 102 / EPC Art. 54) against subsequent corporate enclosure; and (3) Fiduciary Governance Interlocks, linking unauthorized model training directly to corporate director liability under the Delaware Caremark Standard. We establish that willful violation of machine-readable opt-outs constitutes bad-faith governance failure, providing sovereign creators with an actionable, verifiable enforcement shield against predatory algorithmic extraction.

title: Pre-registration: 1-round, 3-seed replication of the QED-gain claim for Conditional GraphGANFed (arXiv 2608.24610) on QM9
abstract: Frozen pre-registration (13 Oct 2026) for a private replication test of one quantitative claim in arXiv 2608.24610, run with the authors' released code (cGraphGANFed d8299d40, GraphGANFed 85d245d6), deposited before the final runs. States the claim, reduced protocol (1 round, 3 seeds: 11-13), every patch to the released code, the evaluator, the decision rule and its planted-effect control, and what was seen beforehand. Includes the finding that the released code does not federate. Repository commit a0a48d04 of the AegisMind analysis tree. No results exist at deposit time.

title: Tecnología en máquinas de venta automatizadas, retail automatizado y quioscos de autoservicio: análisis bibliométrico de la literatura científica desde 1994 hasta 2024
abstract: Las máquinas expendedoras han evolucionado hacia sistemas automatizados mediante la integración de tecnologías digitales, inteligencia artificial y soluciones de autoservicio. Este estudio tiene como objetivo analizar las tendencias investigativas sobre tecnología de máquinas de ventas mediante un análisis bibliométrico de la literatura científica publicada entre 1994 y 2024. La investigación siguió los lineamientos de la declaración PRISMA-2020 y utilizó información procedente de las bases de datos Scopus y Web of Science, identificando un corpus final de 97 artículos después de aplicar los criterios de selección establecidos. Los resultados evidencian un crecimiento de la producción científica, con un incremento del 99,33% durante el periodo analizado y una mayor concentración de publicaciones en 2023. Asimismo, se identificaron autores, revistas y países con mayor influencia en el campo, además de una evolución temática desde enfoques iniciales relacionados con Technology Mapping hacia tendencias actuales asociadas con Technology Adoption, Virtual Reality, Waste Management y Quick-Service Restaurant. El análisis de coocurrencia permitió identificar nueve clústeres temáticos, mientras que las palabras clave emergentes como Community Change, New Technologies, Customer Value y Sustainability muestran nuevas oportunidades de investigación relacionadas con tecnología, usuarios y sostenibilidad.

title: LAMP: 3D Source-Aware Lighting Estimation at Multiple Points
abstract: Existing illumination estimation methods primarily recover lighting distributions for rendering, but typically leave the contributions of individual physical light sources at specific scene locations implicit. We address this gap by leveraging the scene understanding capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) to connect local illumination with its physical sources. We introduce LAMP, a framework for point-conditioned, source-aware illumination reasoning from a single RGB image with marked query points. LAMP constructs a shared inventory of active light sources, ranks contributing sources for each query, and predicts their 3D query-to-source directions. We supervise these relationships using procedurally controlled indoor scenes, reusing independently rendered source responses to derive contribution targets across lighting configurations and obtaining exact directions from source and query positions. On the Infinigen test set, fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B increases dominant-source 3D PCK@0.5m from 0% to 70.6%, with 94.5% of directions within 12.5 degrees of ground truth among correctly localized sources. Combined with a lightweight network predicting dense RGB irradiance, LAMP achieves probe-rendering quality comparable to prior lighting-estimation methods while additionally localizing individual physical sources in 3D and explicitly attributing local illumination to them.

title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
abstract: Existing machine-learning models for perovskite solar cells struggle to predict devices made from new materials. Most treat device layers as arbitrary categorical labels and represent perovskite absorbers either through featureless composition vectors or through rigid crystal graphs that require a pre-solved unit cell. As a result, they cannot generalize to unrecorded alloys or unfamiliar cell architectures. We present the Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System (V-PaSS), an architecture built around the physical continuity of perovskite solid solutions. V-PaSS represents arbitrary mixed-cation, mixed-halide absorbers by interpolating relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure $ABX_3$ endpoint compounds via Vegard's law with learned bandgap bowing. For the device stack, it couples layer sequence and cell polarity (n-i-p or p-i-n) with interfacial band offsets and encodes chemical descriptions with a scientific language model. Evaluated under an institution-grouped protocol where test devices come exclusively from unseen laboratories, an untuned default configuration of V-PaSS achieves the lowest error among fourteen tested models (2.861% MAE, a 5.2% relative reduction over a gradient-boosted baseline at 3.017%, and outperforming the best tuned benchmark at 2.912%). V-PaSS pulls furthest ahead where test devices differ most from training: reducing error by 15.7-19.0% on unseen absorber alloys, by 16.1% on mixed absorbers from new laboratories, and widening its lead over the baseline by 3.6$\times$ on devices with unobserved transport layers. Combined with tree ensembles, V-PaSS sets a new state of the art across all five benchmark splits.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Graph Transformers for Hierarchical Intention Recognition from Multimodal Human Activity Sequences
abstract: Proactive human-robot collaboration requires autonomous systems to infer not only immediate actions but also the underlying hierarchical intentions governing human behavior. Current deep learning approaches predominantly focus on flat action classification, failing to capture the structural dependencies connecting kinematic motion to high-level goals. A Neuro-Symbolic Graph Transformer (NSGT) is proposed within this multimodal framework, a Human Reasoning Graph (HR-G) is integrated into the self-attention mechanism via learnable topological biases. Furthermore, the architecture is augmented with a differentiable First-Order Logic (FOL) loss, acting as a structural regularizer by which ontological consistency is enforced across four levels: atomic actions, composite activities, Low-Level Intentions, and High-Level Intentions. Evaluation is performed on the synthesized NTU-Hierarchy dataset, a four-level ontological extension of NTU RGB+D 120, wherein existing sequences were mapped into 119,383 complex hierarchical episodes (85 actions, 16 activities, 8 LLIs, 4 HLIs). To prevent circular supervision, strict isolation between label generation and FOL constraints was maintained. In the base configuration, 91.65% top-1 action accuracy is achieved by the NSGT. When the FOL loss is incorporated into the baseline, logic consistency is improved by 3.26 percentage points to 96.67%. Through the HR-G biases, a tunable trade-off between accuracy and structural coherence is established. In the primary consistency-maximizing configuration ($λ$ = 0.5), a logic consistency of 94.59% is reached and ontological contradictions are reduced by 33%, while a robust 89.90% top-1 action accuracy is retained. Finally, interpretable reasoning evidence is provided by the learned HR-G weights, wherein transition edges are strongly exploited ($β$ trans $\approx$ +2.6) without explicit supervision.

title: PUGS: Physics-Guided Uncertainty Modeling for Underwater Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) provides an efficient framework for dynamic scene reconstruction. Most existing approaches model scene dynamics with deterministic deformation fields, assuming each Gaussian follows a distinct geometric trajectory over time. This assumption breaks down underwater, where light scattering, refraction, marine snow and low visibility create substantial physical ambiguity in captured images. We present PUGS, a physics-guided uncertainty model for underwater dynamic 3DGS. PUGS learns inherent uncertainty induced by underwater image formation and leverages it as a physical signal for dynamic scene modeling. Rather than estimating a single deterministic displacement, it parameterizes each Gaussian's motion as a probability distribution with expected deformation and physical uncertainty. We adopt stochastic deformation optimization to sample Gaussian trajectories via local reparameterization, exploring multiple physically plausible solutions during training. We further propose uncertainty stochastic annealing and a dual-path self-consistency distillation objective, converting stochastic exploration to deterministic reconstruction while preserving temporal coherence. Extensive experiments on underwater dynamic datasets and physics-aware benchmarks demonstrate superior rendering quality, temporal consistency and reconstruction robustness. Our method achieves 1.16 dB PSNR gain over the strongest baseline on UVEB and 3.99 dB on DRUVA.

title: Scalable Postselection of Quantum Resources
abstract: The large overhead imposed by quantum error correction is a critical challenge to the realization of quantum computers, and motivates searching for alternative error correcting codes and fault-tolerant circuit constructions. Postselection is a powerful tool that builds large programs out of probabilistically generated sub-circuits, and has been shown to increase the threshold of quantum error correction based on fusing fixed-size resource states or concatenated codes. In this work, we present an approach to lower the overhead of quantum computing using scalable postselection, based on directly postselecting sub-circuits with a size extensive in the code distance using decoder soft information. We introduce a metric, the partial gap, that estimates what the logical gap of a resource state will be after it is consumed, and show that postselection based on the partial gap leads to scalable improvements in the logical error rate. In the specific context of implementing logical gates via teleportation through a cluster state, we demonstrate that scalable postselection provides a $4\times$ reduction in the overhead per logical gate, at the same logical error probability.

title: Sistema de estudio para ingreso a la Escuela Politécnica Nacional: módulo – Asistente de Aprendizaje con LLM Local
abstract: El presente Trabajo de Integración Curricular aborda el diseño e implementación de un asistente de aprendizaje basado en un modelo de lenguaje de gran tamaño (LLM) ejecutado en entorno local, que actúa como componente orquestador de un sistema de tutoría inteligente multi-modelo para la preparación del examen de ingreso a la Escuela Politécnica Nacional. El problema de partida es que los aspirantes enfrentan el proceso de admisión con recursos de preparación heterogéneos y retroalimentación limitada, mientras que las soluciones comerciales basadas en la nube introducen restricciones de privacidad, latencia variable y ausencia de especialización en el currículo institucional. El desarrollo siguió el Modelo de Prototipos a lo largo de cinco iteraciones. En la primera se realizó una evaluación comparativa de cinco modelos de código abierto sobre tres bloques de prueba diseñados a la medida del rol de orquestación, de la que se derivó una arquitectura dual: el modelo qwen2.5:1.5b para la clasificación de consultas y qwen2.5:14b para el análisis de desempeño y la generación de rutas de aprendizaje, ambos cuantizados en formato GGUF Q4_K_M y ejecutados mediante Ollama en un servidor CPU sin GPU. En las iteraciones siguientes se implementó una API REST con FastAPI que expone los flujos de clasificación, planificación y retroalimentación; se construyó un pipeline de recuperación aumentada por generación (RAG) sobre los documentos oficiales de admisión, con embeddings multilingües almacenados en ChromaDB; y se integró el módulo con el backend Node.js/TypeScript y los modelos especialistas numérico y verbal. Las pruebas funcionales y de integración end-to-end confirmaron que el sistema completo opera de forma coordinada, desde la consulta del estudiante hasta la persistencia de la decisión académica, con latencias síncronas tolerables en la clasificación y asíncronas aceptables en la generación de planes con contexto institucional. La evaluación de la calidad del contenido generado, estructurada según los criterios del marco RAGAS, evidenció una alta pertinencia de las rutas propuestas y permitió elevar la fidelidad al contexto recuperado mediante la descomposición de la tarea de generación en dos pasos. Los resultados validan la viabilidad de construir tutores inteligentes anclados al currículo institucional sin depender de servicios en la nube ni de hardware GPU, preservando la privacidad de los datos del estudiante dentro de la infraestructura de la institución.

title: Quantum Key Distribution over Free Space Optical Satellite Links in the 6G Era
abstract: Satellite-based free-space optical links can act as time-varying optical wireless interconnects that distribute quantum resources across space-terrestrial infrastructures, complementing the 6G vision of integrated non-terrestrial networks. Among quantum communication services, Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is the most mature and is therefore adopted as an illustrative use case. This paper develops an attenuation-centric framework for satellite QKD based on weak-coherentpulse BB84. The considered system model links orbital geometry and optical terminal parameters to an equivalent channel transmissivity, which governs detection statistics, quantum bit error rate (QBER), and secret key generation through secrecy bounds. We derive the secret-fraction cutoff behavior with respect to channel attenuation and show how it induces time-dependent secret key rates during satellite overpasses. Numerical results using orbital data and representative parameters from the 'Micius' mission show that the minimum slant range over the onemonth observation window spans approximately 400-2400 km; approximately 34% of passes have minimum slant ranges below 900 km, and favorable passes yield secret key rates on the order of a few kbps. The proposed modeling approach provides a link-level building block for future network-level studies, where scheduling and routing of quantum-secured services can be informed by predicted key generation windows over satellite optical interconnects.

title: Selecting the 7th Smallest of 16 Elements Takes Exactly 28 Comparisons: code, certificates and Lean proofs
abstract: First release of the research artifacts accompanying: Jonathan Cremer, Selecting the 7th Smallest of 16 Elements Takes Exactly 28 Comparisons. Includes: Explicit comparison-algorithm certificates for all seven new upper bounds. An independent static verifier, execution tests, and an exact path oracle. Lean 4 proofs of all seven numerical upper bounds. A separate Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of the analytical lower-bound theory. Search code and scripts for the evaluations reported in the paper. The published numerical lower bounds used to establish the exact values are credited in the README. Build and verification instructions are provided in the respective code directories.

title: Homomorphic Functional Encryption: Trustless Key Derivation for Functional Encryption
abstract: In this paper, we study the trust assumptions underlying key generation in functional encryption (FE) schemes, as well as the information leakage that can arise from the use of functional decryption keys. FE schemes typically rely on a trusted key curator who holds the master secret key and derives functional decryption keys. This requirement makes the curator a central point of trust and a particularly sensitive target for compromise. We show how homomorphic encryption (HE) can be used to mitigate this problem by allowing FE key-derivation algorithms to be evaluated homomorphically. Building on the function-blind key derivation approach of Canard et al., we extend this approach to a three-party deployment in which the key curator does not hold the FE master secret key in the clear. The resulting construction preserves function blindness against a semi-honest key curator while protecting the master secret key from the curator, thereby reducing the trust assumptions associated with conventional FE key management. Additionally, to evaluate the feasibility of our approach, we developed a proof-of-concept implementation and ran a series of benchmarks. The large parameter set requires 335.7 seconds for encrypted key derivation. Finally, as a way to support open science and reproducible research, we make our code publicly available.
